name: Ghent
title: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement Ghent | Bulk Carriers
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Ghent: bulk carrier hold and hull structure UTM, ESP renewal survey support and pre-purchase gauging at the canal port.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Bulk Carriers and Ships in Ghent
intro: Ghent is reached only by the canal from Terneuzen, and the ships that make that passage come for steel, grain, forest products and cars. Bulk carriers discharging iron ore and coal at the steelworks are the core of the port's gauging work: hold frames, hopper plating and topside tanks take punishment on every call. Superintendents use us for UTM in Ghent before intermediate and renewal surveys, and every ship is attended by technicians mobilised from India.

highlights.h: Holds after ore and coal discharge
highlights.p: Bulk carriers at the steelworks quay leave with holds swept and empty. That short window is the best time for hold-frame, bracket and hopper gauging, before ballast is taken and the ship sails for its next cargo.

highlights.h: A canal port with predictable stays
highlights.p: The Terneuzen locks and the canal passage mean ships call for whole cargo operations rather than quick stops, and berth times are planned. Gauging can be scheduled against a known discharge or loading plan.
Ro-ro ships loading cars and trailers, and handysize bulkers handling grain and oilseeds, offer deck, ramp, hold and hatch-coaming gauging on their regular calls at the Ghent docks.

port.h: Ghent: a canal port for steel, bulk and ro-ro
p: Ghent is the inland end of North Sea Port. Ships enter from the Westerschelde through the sea locks at Terneuzen and follow the Ghent–Terneuzen canal south across the Dutch–Belgian border to docks on the northern side of the city. The canal limits the size of ship that can call, so the bulk carriers seen here are smaller than the ore carriers that discharge at Rotterdam, and the fleet is made up of mid-sized bulk carriers, ro-ro ships, general cargo ships and product tankers. The cargo base is industrial: iron ore and coal for the ArcelorMittal steelworks, grain and oilseeds for processing plants, forest products, fertilisers, biofuels and vehicles. Inland barges share the canal, carrying cargo on into the Belgian and French waterway network.

The canal passage changes how ships use the port. Lock slots and canal pilotage make arrival and departure planned events, and a bulk carrier coming to Ghent normally stays for its whole discharge rather than lightening and moving on. Ro-ro services to Scandinavia run on regular rotations from the Ghent docks, and agribulk ships often wait between discharge and their next fixture. Those patterns give predictable windows: the time between end of discharge and sailing, a lay period alongside, or the hours a ro-ro ship spends between rotations.

Inspection demand therefore centres on bulk carriers. They are ESP ships under IACS UR Z10.2 (single-side skin) or Z10.5 (double-skin), and the ore and coal trade wears them in predictable places: hold frames and their brackets, lower stools and hopper plating, hatch coamings, and the topside and hopper ballast tanks. Coal cargoes add corrosion of hold steel where moisture and sulphur combine. Ships on this trade face intermediate surveys with close-up and thickness requirements, and a superintendent who gauges them at Ghent can plan steel well ahead of the yard.

facilities.h: Where gauging fits along the Ghent docks and canal
p: The steelworks quays on the canal are the most frequent setting for bulk carrier gauging in Ghent. Once the grabs have finished and the holds are swept, the ship provides lighting and access, and the team works through frames, brackets and hopper plating to the TM plan, adding the topside and hopper tanks where the crew can de-ballast and ventilate them before departure. Agribulk and forest-product terminals give similar windows on smaller bulk carriers and general cargo ships. Hull gauging in Ghent beyond the holds, such as deck plating and ballast tank structure, depends on what the crew can empty and ventilate during the call.

Ghent is not a dry-docking centre for deep-sea ships, so dockings are usually planned elsewhere — Vlissingen, Antwerp or further afield — and the Ghent call is used for pre-docking gauging that sizes the steel list. Readings taken here travel with the ship and are recorded in a form the docking yard can use directly. Ro-ro berths serving the Scandinavian services, and the car terminal, suit deck and ramp gauging during lay periods. Tankers loading or discharging biofuels and oil products at the canal-side tank terminals work under terminal permits, with tank entry only when the ship is gas-free.
list: Steelworks ore and coal quays — hold frame, bracket, hopper and hatch coaming gauging on bulk carriers between end of discharge and sailing.
Agribulk terminals — hold, tank-top and ballast tank readings on handysize and supramax bulkers after a grain or oilseed discharge.
Forest products and general cargo berths — hatch cover, coaming and tween-deck gauging on multipurpose and open-hatch ships.
Ro-ro and car terminal berths — main-deck, ramp and car-deck gauging on ro-ro ships during lay periods between rotations.
Canal-side tank terminals — manifold and deck-line wall thickness on product and biofuel tankers, with cargo tanks left until a gas-free certificate is issued.

context.h: Steel trade, emissions rules and port state control in Ghent
p: Ghent's ships fall under Paris MoU port state control as callers at a Belgian port, and the canal and the Westerschelde approaches lie in the North Sea SOx ECA, and compliant 0.10% sulphur fuel or a scrubber is needed for the whole passage. Under the Paris MoU an older bulk carrier is a candidate for an expanded inspection, and hold damage from grabs and corrosion is easy for an inspector to see. Arriving with recent gauging and documented repairs puts the master in a better position if a port state control officer looks into the holds.

Decarbonisation plans for the steel and chemical industry along the canal, together with port and industry projects in hydrogen, carbon capture and biofuels, will change Ghent's cargo flows over time. Ore and coal carriers will keep calling meanwhile, and the owners of those older Panamax and supramax bulkers are weighing the carbon obligations that arrived with EU ETS for shipping in 2024 and with FuelEU Maritime a year later against the steel renewal due at the next renewal survey. Gauging supplies the steel side of that judgement, and a Ghent discharge, with empty holds and a planned berth time, is a sensible place to collect it.

jobs.h: Gauging scopes that suit a Ghent call
jobs.p: Because ships in Ghent stay for a full cargo operation, scopes can be larger than at a coastal terminal, but they still end when the ship sails. A good Ghent job is planned around the discharge or loading sequence, with the most important spaces measured first and the report ready before departure. Where a docking follows, the readings are prepared for the docking yard as well. Typical scopes include:
list: A Panamax bulk carrier after discharging ore at the steelworks: hold frames, brackets and hopper plating in all holds, ahead of its second renewal survey.
A supramax bulker after a coal cargo: hold-side and tank-top gauging in holds showing coal-related corrosion, plus topside tank readings if the tanks can be emptied.
A ro-ro ship on a Scandinavian service: main-deck plating and ramp structure gauged during a lay period, with magnetic particle testing at the ramp hinges.
A product tanker discharging biofuel at a canal-side terminal: deck piping, manifold and pump-room line wall-thickness checks under the terminal permit.
A buyer's pre-purchase gauging of a handysize bulker at an agribulk berth: holds, hatch coamings and accessible ballast tanks measured before the sale closes.

logistics: Brussels Airport is the nearest large international gateway, and Ghent is reachable from it by road or by train; Amsterdam Schiphol is an alternative when Dutch-side work in Terneuzen is combined. Port terminals are ISPS-controlled, and the agent arranges gate passes for the berth and confirms the canal arrival time. A team travelling from India needs Schengen visas, which we start on once you confirm the ship's expected call; with lock and canal timings involved, we keep the mobilisation date linked to the agent's updates.

faqs.q: How much hold gauging can be done between discharge and sailing in Ghent?
faqs.a: That depends on the number of holds, the cleaning time and how long the ship stays after the grabs finish. We plan the sequence with the superintendent beforehand, most critical holds and frames first, and set the team size so the planned scope fits the window. Anything not reached is identified clearly in the report rather than left as a silent gap.

faqs.q: Do the Terneuzen locks affect scheduling?
faqs.a: Yes. Ships reach Ghent only through the Terneuzen locks and the canal, so arrival depends on lock slots and pilotage. Travel is booked against the agent's latest estimate, and we stay flexible as it moves. Once the ship is alongside in Ghent, the cargo plan rather than the lock decides the working window.

faqs.q: Can a Ghent gauging job prepare for a docking elsewhere?
faqs.a: Often it is the best use of the call. A steel estimate gathered in the holds and tanks at Ghent goes with the docking specification to whichever yard the owner chooses, so competing yards are compared on the same measured basis and steel can be ordered before the ship arrives.

faqs.q: Do you check hatch covers and coamings on bulk carriers?
faqs.a: Yes. Hatch coamings, coaming stays and hatch cover plating are gauged with the hold programme, and cracking at coaming brackets can be checked by magnetic particle testing. On ships in the ore and coal trade those areas see impact and corrosion, and their condition matters for weathertightness as well as for structural strength.
